Re: Michael Brooks (DOB 12/20/1964)

Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to provide a medical summary for Mr. Michael Brooks, who has been under my care at Rogers-Parrish Medical Group since his diagnosis of Type 2 diabetes in March 2022. Below is a detailed account of his medical history, current condition, and treatment plan.

Mr. Brooks was diagnosed with Type 2 diabetes on March 2, 2022, at the age of 57. Since then, he has been closely monitored and managed for his condition. As of the most recent visit on July 21, 2025, Mr. Brooks continues to be under my care for his Type 2 diabetes. During this visit, his blood pressure was recorded at 127/77, and his weight was 182 pounds. His overall condition remains stable and well-controlled.

On December 6, 2024, Mr. Brooks visited for routine follow-up regarding his Type 2 diabetes. His blood pressure was 124/76, and his weight was 188 pounds. At this visit, Mr. Brooks reported no significant complaints and appeared to be doing well. His A1C level at that time was 7.5, indicating good glycemic control.

In April 2024, Mr. Brooks presented with a rash. blood pressure was 116/76, and his weight was 178 pounds. The rash was evaluated, and appropriate treatment was initiated. Mr. Brooks's Type 2 diabetes remained stable, with an A1C level of 7.5.

On September 8, 2023, Mr. Brooks visited for a strain. His blood pressure was 117/80, and his weight was 190 pounds. The back strain was and was given appropriate recommendations for relief and recovery. His Type 2 diabetes was noted with an A1C level of 7.4 at this visit.

The initial diagnosis of Type diabetes was confirmed on January 24, 2023. Mr. Brooks's blood pressure was 116/80, and his weight was 186 pounds. At this visit, his A1C level was 7.4, indicating good control of his blood glucose levels. The duration of his diabetes at this point was 3.9 years, with an average A1C of 7.4 over the period.

Mr. Brooks has been compliant with his treatment regimen, which includes metformin 1000 mg and empagliflozin 25 mg. His A1C trend over the past year has shown consistent levels, with readings of 7.5 in July 2025, 7.5 in December 2024, 7.5 in April 2024, and 7.4 in September 2023.

Additionally, Mr. Brooks has a family history of COPD in his mother, who is currently living and well. There is no history of neuropathy, or coronary artery disease associated with his diabetes.

Mr. Brooks has been an active individual, exercising regularly. He reports running 3-4 times a week, which has likely contributed t

o his overall health and management of diabetes. 

In terms of social history, Mr. Brooks was a former cigarette smoker who smoked one pack per day starting from April 29, 2015. He successfully quit smoking on June 10, 2024, and has since minimized any tobacco use. Regarding alcohol consumption, he reports consuming approximately 6 drinks per week, which is within moderate limits.

His vital signs have been within normal ranges throughout his visits, with blood pressure readings of 127/77, 124/76, 116/76, 117/80, and 116/80, and weights of 182, 188, 178, 190, and 186 pounds, respectively.

Mr. Brooks continues to be under regular follow-up for his Type 2 diabetes. His condition is well-managed, and he adheres to medication and lifestyle recommendations.

If you have any further questions or require additional information, please do not hesitate to contact me.

Sincerely,

Dr. William Collins, MD
Endocrinology
Rogers-Parrish Medical Group
